title: Enhancing Population-based Search with Active Inference

abstract: We propose integrating Active Inference into population-based metaheuristics to enhance performance through anticipatory environmental adaptation. Demonstrated with Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) on the Travelling Salesman Problem (TSP), experimental results indicate Active Inference yields improved solutions with marginal increase in computational cost, with performance patterns relating to graph topology.

methods.name: Active Inference-augmented Ant Colony Optimization for the TSP
methods.description: ACO is extended with a belief-update mechanism and a free-energy calculation so ant node selection adapts to current tour quality.
methods.evidence: Our algorithm introduces a belief update mechanism and free energy calculation, enabling adaptive decision-making based on the cur- rent tour quality.

methods.name: Belief-weighted node selection and free-energy tour scoring
methods.description: Belief is set from current versus best path length, scales pheromone/distance selection probabilities, and enters a free energy of path length plus entropy.
methods.evidence: computes the free energy for a given tour, combining the expected path length and associated uncertainty:

methods.name: Benchmark against basic ACO and Nearest Neighbor on random symmetric graphs
methods.description: The AI-enhanced ACO was compared to basic ACO and a Nearest Neighbor heuristic on randomly generated symmetric graphs of several sizes.
methods.evidence: we conducted a series of experiments comparing it against a basic ACO, and a baseline Nearest Neighbor heuristic (NN).

methods.name: Paired t-test, Wilcoxon signed-rank, and Mann-Whitney U tests
methods.description: Tour length and computation time differences between basic and AI-enhanced ACO were assessed with paired and non-parametric tests.
methods.evidence: Paired T-test for Tour Length: T-statistic = 2.7852, P-value = 0.00641

methods.evidence: Python implementations of the variaous methods considered in our experiments are provided in the Appendix of this manuscript.

key_findings: The Active Inference-enhanced ACO gave mean tour-length improvements over basic ACO at every graph size tested, peaking at 8.81% for 100-node graphs.
Relative computational overhead fell with graph size, from 9.46% at 25 nodes to 1.97% at 500 nodes.
Tour-length improvements were significant by paired t-test and Wilcoxon test, but the Mann-Whitney U test found no significant difference in overall distributions.
The computation-time difference was not statistically significant at the 0.05 level.
The authors note high variability in tour lengths for both algorithms, with performance gains varying considerably across graph types.
key_findings_evidence: For 25-node graphs, the average improvement was 2.52%. This improvement increased to 3.62% for 50-node graphs and rose significantly to 8.81% for 100- node graphs.
